research.currentNameReassessment:
"Random Thought Organizer" now describes the general product accurately: capture stray thoughts, then organize, connect and clarify them. It also carries the lowest legal and namespace risk of anything screened, but it works better as a descriptor than as the brand.

Legal and namespace position, checked 2026-09-25:
- **USPTO:** no live mark in any class. RANDOM THOUGHTS has 4 filings, all dead (classes 3, 16, 41 and 16). THOUGHT ORGANIZER and randomthought* return 0 filings (tmsearch backend).
- **Domains:** randomthoughtorganizer.app and .com are both unregistered (RDAP 404).
- **npm:** random-thought-organizer is free.
- **MCP registry:** no thought or notes "organizer" server.

Why it is weak as a brand:
1. **Merely descriptive.** A US application would likely be refused on the Principal Register or need a disclaimer, and it cannot stop others using the phrase. The phrase is already in use: iOS "Mindscope - Thought Organizer" and "Idea Think: Thought Organizer" (Productivity), Google Play "Quick Notes: Thought Organizer" and "Brain Dump - Organize Thoughts", and a Notion template called "Brain Dump: A Thought Organizer".
2. **It names the input, not the payoff.** The AI connecting, clarifying and briefing is invisible.
3. **Hard to find.** It competes on generic keywords, the Organizer/Organiser spelling splits search, and at 24 characters it is too long for a slash command or package name.

No good short handle comes from the phrase itself. RTO is blocked (Return to Office, Recovery Time Objective, India's RTO apps, live RTO marks). Other abbreviations such as RTOrg or RandO are ugly. "/thoughts" is generic and likely to collide with other skills.

Verdict: keep the phrase as the lowercase product descriptor (store subtitle, plugin description, SEO line) under a coined brand, for example "Mullwise, the random thought organizer", with the brand as the handle (/mull or /mullwise).

Method limits:
- The automated batch screen, which used the gh CLI, was denied by the permission system, and one later detailed USPTO query was also denied.
- GitHub evidence below comes from web search only, not the GitHub API. No per-name GitHub user or org handle check was done.
- Where live-mark details beyond classes 9/42 are missing, they are marked unverified.

This is not legal clearance.

shortlist.name: Mullwise
shortlist.why: It is the cleanest name found in every channel checked. There is no app on either US store (Play says 'No results'), zero USPTO filings, and npm and the MCP registry are clear. Both mullwise.app and mullwise.com were unregistered on 2026-09-25. It evokes mulling stray thoughts ('mull') and AI clarity ('-wise'), covers every subject kind (topic, person, talk, decision, project), and gives a short natural handle, /mull. It extends the earlier 'Mulled' pick, whose .app was taken, into a coined, ownable word.
shortlist.risks:
- **Shared root:** 'Mull' is shared with a small Google Play app, 'MULL - Save & Resurface' (mariosu), which does adjacent save-and-resurface. Mullvad VPN also starts with 'Mull', and the discontinued Mull browser used the word.
- **npm:** 'mull' is taken by an empty 2017 placeholder, so the package would be named 'mullwise'.
- **Unchecked marks:** standalone 'MULL' USPTO marks in 9/42 were not checked.
- **Discoverability:** the name does not say 'notes', so it needs the descriptor line.
- **Suffix:** '-wise' is a common software suffix (Splitwise, Typewise), which weakens distinctiveness a little.
- **Domains:** register them yourself; nothing was purchased.
shortlist.tagline: Mullwise: your random thought organizer. Drop a thought; it connects the dots.

shortlist.name: Stray Thoughts
shortlist.why: The most immediately understood name for the general product. It is warm, human and accurate. USPTO has zero filings, no app uses the name on either US store, straythoughts.app is unregistered, and npm 'stray-thoughts' is free. It reads well in a Claude skill trigger ('save this stray thought').
shortlist.risks:
- **Weak mark:** it is a common phrase already used by blogs, a podcast and a Substack, so it would be hard to own in search or enforce.
- **Domain:** straythoughts.com is held and locked (registered 2014).
- **Other uses:** 'Stray' is a popular video game.
- **Undersells the AI:** it does not signal the connecting and clarifying.
shortlist.tagline: Every stray thought, caught, connected, and clarified.

shortlist.name: Brainlint
shortlist.why: Distinctive and playful, with zero USPTO filings and no app on either store. brainlint.app is unregistered, npm 'brainlint' is free, and there are no MCP collisions. The 'lint' joke ('tidies up your thinking') lands with the developer audience that meets a Claude plugin first.
shortlist.risks:
- **Domain:** brainlint.com is held (registered 2007).
- **Name holder:** a small Canadian theatre company uses 'Brain Lint Productions'.
- **Tone:** 'lint' can read as worthless fluff, or be mistaken for a code linter, and is less inviting for non-technical users later.
shortlist.tagline: Pick the fluff out of your head. Keep the good stuff, connected.

shortlist.name: Bowerbird
shortlist.why: The best metaphor on the list. The bowerbird collects scattered objects and arranges them into a meaningful display, which covers capture plus AI organizing in one image. The only software mark (class 9 database software) is cancelled, npm is free, the MCP registry is clear, and no note-taking app uses the name.
shortlist.risks:
- **Domains:** bowerbird.app (2018) and bowerbird.com (1998) are both taken, so you would need a variant such as getbowerbird.app (not checked).
- **Existing apps:** iOS apps use the name (AI Real Estate Agent, Flashcards) and bowerbird.io is an AI publicity app for architects.
- **Live marks:** BOWERBIRD PHOTOGRAPHY (cl.41) and GREAT BOWERBIRDLING DESIGN (cl.40/42).
- **Length:** three syllables, and a less obvious handle (/bower).
shortlist.tagline: Collects your stray thoughts. Arranges them into something clear.

shortlist.name: Random Thought Organizer (as descriptor)
shortlist.why: It now describes the product exactly and carries the least legal risk. There is no live mark for the phrase in any class, randomthoughtorganizer.app and .com are both unregistered, and npm is free. It is the right words for App Store subtitles, plugin descriptions and SEO, and it preserves the RTO codename's meaning.
shortlist.risks:
- **Unprotectable:** it is merely descriptive, so others can't be stopped from using it.
- **Crowded:** 'Thought Organizer' apps already exist (Mindscope, Idea Think, Quick Notes).
- **Hides the AI:** it doesn't show the connect and clarify value.
- **Unwieldy:** too long for a handle, and RTO is unusable publicly. Use it only as the descriptor under a brand.
shortlist.tagline: Capture any thought. AI connects, clarifies, and briefs you.

research.recommendation:
Recommendation: public brand **Mullwise**, with the descriptor "random thought organizer", for example "Mullwise: your random thought organizer". Use /mull (or /mullwise) as the Claude skill handle, 'mullwise' as the plugin, npm and MCP server name, and keep RTO as the internal codename only.

**Why Mullwise:** it was the only brandable candidate clean on every surface checked.
- No app of that name on the US App Store (iTunes Search API) or US Google Play ('No results for mullwise').
- Zero USPTO filings for MULLWISE or MULL WISE. MULLED marks are food and drink only.
- Both mullwise.app and mullwise.com were unregistered on 2026-09-25 (RDAP 404).
- npm 'mullwise' is free, and there are no MCP registry or Anthropic Directory hits.
It also carries the owner's earlier 'Mulled' instinct into a coined, ownable word that fits every subject kind, not just conversation prep.

**Runners-up:**
- **Stray Thoughts:** the most self-explanatory. Weak as a mark because the phrase is common; .app free, .com taken.
- **Brainlint:** playful and developer-friendly. .app free, .com taken.
- **Bowerbird:** the best metaphor, but both domains are taken and it has medium store noise.

**Avoid (high conflict):**
- **Threadle:** npm and GitHub Claude Code tool, updated 2026-09-23.
- **Asterism:** GitHub Claude Code tool for 'scattered notes'.
- **Skein:** 'Skein Notes' Mac PKM app plus a live class 9/42 SKEIN mark.
- **Weft:** 'Weft: Stay in Touch' people-notebook app plus live class 42 WEFT marks.
- **Dotwise:** dotwise.app personal knowledge system plus a live class 9 mark.
- **Knotebook:** two GitHub note apps, one AI-based.
- **Thinkloom:** a GitHub LLM knowledge platform.
- **Red String, Marginalia, Commonplace:** each has several apps or tools of the same name.

**Medium conflict:** Thought Threads, See Also, Decant, Scholia, Unmuddle, Orbweaver, Flotsam, Strandline.

**Next steps before any public listing:**
1. Register mullwise.app and mullwise.com yourself. Nothing was purchased.
2. Run a full USPTO search, including standalone MULL marks in classes 9, 42 and 35, and phonetic variants (Mulwise, Mullwize). Add EUIPO, UKIPO and WIPO.
3. Check GitHub user and org availability for 'mullwise' and the community Claude plugin marketplaces by hand.
4. If the product will be sold, consider a low-cost attorney knockout search.

**Method limits, stated honestly:**
- Stores were checked through the iTunes Search API (US) and Google Play search with the US storefront parameters.
- Domains were checked through the Google Registry and Verisign RDAP. USPTO was checked through the tmsearch backend, on wordmarks only.
- The automated batch screen, which used the user's authenticated gh CLI, was denied by the permission system. A later detailed USPTO query was also denied. So GitHub evidence comes from web search only (no API or handle checks), and some live-mark details for Flotsam, Marginalia, Red String and Skein are unverified. The user can allow those if a fuller re-run is wanted.
- The Claude plugin check covered the in-session Anthropic Directory search only. Community directories (claudemarketplaces.com, claude-plugins.dev) could not be queried by name.

verification.summary:
I re-checked 25 of the most decision-relevant claims using RDAP, the npm registry, the MCP registry, the iTunes Search API, Google Play pages, the GitHub API, web search and the USPTO tmsearch backend (phrase and prefix queries on wordmarks).

**Mullwise holds up.** mullwise.app and mullwise.com are still unregistered. USPTO has 0 filings for MULLWISE, MULLWIZE, MULWISE or the prefix mullwis*. Neither US app store has an app of that name. npm and the MCP registry are clear. The GitHub handle 'mullwise' is free.

**The standalone MULL mark gap is now closed.** No live MULL-formative mark covers software or SaaS. The live marks are cl.12 trailer hitch covers, cl.25 clothing, and cl.9 music recordings (MULL GRAHAM).

**The main new risk is the Google Play app 'MULL - Save & Resurface'.** It is an on-device, no-account, privacy-first app for saving, notes and resurfacing, with a paid sync plan, and it appears as 'Mull' in the share sheet. That positioning is closer to RTO's than 'adjacent', so it argues for /mullwise over /mull as the handle. Also, mull.app is registered and mull.ai is for sale.

**The runner-ups check out.** Stray Thoughts, Brainlint and the Random Thought Organizer descriptor all match on USPTO, domains and npm.

**Corrections:**
- **RANDOM THOUGHTS:** 3 exact filings, not 4. Serial 85788036 is 'RANDIM THOUGHTS AND EXPRESSIONS'.
- **Bowerbird:** the research omitted 5 live standalone BOWERBIRD marks, none in software classes.
- **Dotwise:** dotwise.app is an AI learning-course product, not a personal notes organizer, so 'direct functional conflict' is overstated. The live cl.9 mark still stands.
- **Thinkloom:** the cited GitHub repo is 404. Other Thinkloom repos exist.
- **MULLED:** marks are not food and drink only; they include cosmetics, candles and air fresheners. None is in 9/42.
- **Knotebook:** the release details are outdated; the repo is now at v0.4.1.

**Confirmed high-conflict avoids:** Threadle (npm/GitHub Claude Code tool updated 2026-09-23), Asterism, Skein and Weft.

**Missed competitor:** Einfall, a 2026 privacy-first thought-capture app that routes thoughts to AI agents through a local MCP server.

**Still unverified:** non-US trademark clearance for Mullwise.

This is not legal clearance.

research.whitespace: No product combines all six of RTO's pieces: (1) a one-line 'subject: detail' capture grammar with an AI-guessed subject, (2) AI cross-references labelled as AI-made, (3) a single approval queue for renames, merges and splits, (4) action-oriented recall views (open-items checklist, decision tree, talk-time checklist with outcome capture), (5) an encrypted local store, (6) delivery inside Claude. Neighbors each cover a slice. obsidian-second-brain has person, decision and project notes, scheduled digests and dry-run merges, but it is a 45-command power tool that needs Obsidian, a CLI agent and unencrypted files. Lightnote has dump, auto-tag and daily insights, but it is cloud-only, tags without review and has no structure. The new Tana has merge proposals and approve-before-write MCP, but it is a team meeting platform. Capacities has typed objects and an official MCP server, but typing is manual and data lives in the cloud. Smart Dedupe Pro has review-first merges, but only inside an Obsidian plugin. Reflect has end-to-end encryption with only a selected slice sent to AI, but no automatic organizing. No surveyed product offered a decision-tree or talk-time checklist view. Market signals point to the defensible position: generic 'chat with your notes' is losing to the big labs (Khoj Cloud shut down Apr 15 2026 citing lab competition; Reor archived Mar 7 2026), and Claude memory, Google Keep Live and Apple Notes AI are absorbing basic capture and summarizing. The open space is trusted, reviewable structure over the owner's own thoughts, private by default and inside the assistant the owner already uses.
differentiationIdeas: Make approval the product: one 'Proposals' inbox for every AI-made link, rename, merge, split and subject guess. Each shows its reason, the evidence thoughts and a confidence, with approve, reject or edit in one step. Remember rejections so the same suggestion is not made again.
Label provenance everywhere (owner-made or AI-made, and when) and make every AI change reversible through an undo log. Merged subjects leave redirects and aliases, never deletions.

Treat the capture grammar as the moat. 'Budget: ask Sam…' fuzzy-matches existing subjects and aliases. With no subject, RTO proposes one inline. The kind (person, talk, decision, project) is inferred from cues such as names, 'decide', 'meet' or 'call', and the owner confirms it once per subject.

Action-first recall, which no note app surveyed offers: per-subject one-glance brief, open-items checklist, options and decision tree, and for talks a talk-time checklist that captures outcomes afterwards.
Precision over volume in linking: cap the number of AI cross-references per thought, show 'why linked' in one line, and let each digest report link acceptance rate so the thresholds tune themselves.

Privacy people can check: an encrypted local store (Obsidian/Anytype-grade) and send Claude only the slice of subjects a request needs (Reflect's highlight-only pattern). State plainly what leaves the device.
A digest built for hygiene, not just resurfacing: new connections, pending renames and merges, stale subjects, open questions, and decisions with no outcome yet.

Present RTO as working alongside Claude memory: memory personalizes Claude, RTO is the explicit, exportable record the owner controls. Offer to write a short pointer into Claude memory only with the owner's approval.
Zero lock-in: plain Markdown or JSON export at any time, importers from Drafts, Apple Notes and Twos, and an 'open in Obsidian' view.
Pricing matched to micro-capture: no per-note quotas (unlike Mem's 25-2000 notes a month). AI work runs on the owner's own Claude plan.
featureIdeasToBorrow: Tana (new): compare new input against the existing graph and issue a 'merge proposal' instead of appending; MCP writes become proposals that need approval (https://tana.inc/).
Smart Dedupe Pro: review near-duplicates with four choices (keep separate, merge, archive, ignore); 'similar notes can be useful neighbors' (https://smartconnections.app/smart-dedupe/).

obsidian-second-brain: merges dry-run by default and leave redirects; a bounded background agent that can never delete or merge on its own; scheduled morning, nightly, weekly and health runs; a formal decision record option (https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain).

claude-obsidian: an operation plan shown before any change is applied; a lint pass for orphans and dead links; contradictions stay visible instead of being overwritten (https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian).
Lightnote: a swipeable Daily Insights briefing and a weekly reflection letter as the digest format (https://lightnote.ink/).
Evernote: suggest a title only when none was given, with accept, edit or dismiss (https://evernote.com/user-stories/how-auto-generated-titles-mean-a-user-never-has-to-name-a).
Mem: a 'Heads Up' side panel showing related subjects while one is open; organizing starts only when the user asks (https://help.mem.ai/features/collections).

Voicethoughts / Keep Live: split one ramble into several atomic thoughts, each with its own subject, before filing (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/voicethoughts-ai-brain-dump/id6745749081; https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/workspace/voice-features-gmail-docs-keep/).
Twos: capture from anywhere (email, WhatsApp, Raycast, watch) and auto-classify each entry as a to-do or a note, which maps onto RTO's open items (https://www.twosapp.com/).
Capacities: typed objects with a 'Related Content' view of unlinked mentions, mapping to RTO's subject kinds (https://capacities.io/).

Basic Memory: plain Markdown plus a local SQLite index, and categorized observations like [question] or [decision] that could tag open items and options (https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory).
Dex / Granola: build a pre-talk brief from the calendar that feeds the 'talk' kind (https://getdex.com/pricing; https://www.granola.ai/).
Reflect: end-to-end encryption with an independent audit, sending AI only the text the owner selected (https://reflect.academy/artificial-intelligence).
Recall / Napkin: spaced resurfacing, used here to bring stale subjects back in the digest (https://www.recall.it/pricing; https://www.napkin.one/).
pitfallsSeenInMarket: Users distrust auto-organization they cannot inspect. Mem reviews quote 'Tagged items don't always appear when you search for that tag' (compiled by competitor Saner.ai, so vendor-biased: https://www.saner.ai/blogs/mem-ai-reviews). A mymind review says search misses obvious things and Spaces cannot be steered by hand (https://www.marqly.com/blog/mymind-review-2026).

Link noise: a Smart Connections issue reports irrelevant related notes and was closed as not planned (https://github.com/brianpetro/obsidian-smart-connections/issues/907). Smart Dedupe's own copy warns that similarity is not duplication.

AI rewrites with no review. Mem Chat carries out collection merges and cleanup on command with no staged review (https://get.mem.ai/blog/ai-knowledge-base-refactoring). Notion Autofill can re-run on every page edit (https://www.notion.com/help/autofill). My inference: this risks silently overwriting the owner's structure.

Products dying or pivoting leave users stranded. Khoj Cloud shut down on Apr 15 2026 (https://app.khoj.dev/). Reor was archived on Mar 7 2026 (https://github.com/reorproject/reor). Tana pivoted to meetings and renamed its original app 'Tana Outliner' (https://tana.inc/). Voicenotes now sells itself as a meeting notetaker (https://voicenotes.com/). Small apps go stale: Brain Dump last updated Aug 2024, Voicethoughts July 2025.
Quota and credit pricing punishes frequent small captures: Mem Free allows 25 new notes a month and Plus 50 (https://get.mem.ai/pricing), and Tana, Heptabase and Capacities all meter AI credits.

'Private' claims that only mean cloud encryption at rest. mymind does not claim end-to-end encryption (https://mymind.com/data-security). Heptabase is not end-to-end and indexes content with third parties (https://support.heptabase.com/en/articles/10448141-is-my-data-safe-in-heptabase).
Complexity creep: supertag schemas (Tana Outliner) and 45-command skill surfaces (obsidian-second-brain) put off anyone who is not a power user, the opposite of one-line capture.

Big platforms absorbing the basics: Claude memory is free and shared across chat and Cowork (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/25/claude-cowork-finally-remembers-what-you-told-the-app-in-chat/), and Google Keep Live turns rambles into lists (https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/workspace/voice-features-gmail-docs-keep/). Plain capture and summaries are not defensible on their own.

verification.summary:
I checked 30 claims by opening the vendor, GitHub, App Store and support pages cited below. Most product facts hold up: existence, pricing, the Khoj and Reor shutdown dates, the approval features of Tana, Smart Dedupe and claude-obsidian, Claude memory, and Heptabase's privacy model. Nine claims are wrong or overstated:

- **obsidian-second-brain** (the closest rival) has 47 commands and 8 builds, not 45 and 6.
- **It also has phone capture.** A Telegram bot collects captures and /obsidian-catchup files them, so 'no phone path' is wrong.
- **Capacities' MCP server** lists 19 tools, not 17, and is labeled as a Pro feature.
- **Evernote prices** cited from eesel are wrong. The article says $8.25/mo and $20.83/mo, not $14.99 and $24.99.
- **Evernote titles** are applied automatically. They are not offered as accept, edit or dismiss suggestions.
- **Reflect's 'no logs are kept'** overstates it. OpenAI keeps API logs for 30 days, and audio and AI text are not end-to-end encrypted. The Doyensec audit itself is confirmed.
- **Keep Live** needs a paid Google AI plan (Plus, Pro or Ultra).
- **'Reor's archiving leaves no active local auto-link product'** is wrong. Smart Connections is still maintained.
- **The whitespace claim '(6) delivery inside Claude'** is the biggest problem for decisions. Mem has had an official Claude connector for capture, recall and organizing since March 2026. The Mem0 connector is in Anthropic's official directory. Anthropic's own Productivity plugin already tracks people, projects and tasks in Cowork and Claude Code. Hjarni offers a hosted MCP notes store with phone apps. Evernote (beta), Capacities, Tana, Twos, Recall, Voicenotes and Granola all expose MCP.

What still looks defensible is the combination of four things together: approval-gated restructuring, action-oriented recall views (open items, decision tree, talk checklist), true end-to-end or local encryption, and one-line 'subject: detail' capture. Being Claude-native alone is not an advantage.

Two more omissions: ChatGPT's 'Dreaming' memory (June 2026, reorganizes memory by topic in the background) is missing from the platform-risk list, and Supermemory, an auto-linking managed MCP memory service, is not covered.

I could not verify from official pages: Smart Connections Pro and Anytype prices, Recall's storage model, and whether Heptabase has shipped agent tagging since May.
